sentences.text: The species Palintropus retusus is known from a single proximal coracoid bone discovered in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
The type species Palintropus retusus is based on a proximal coracoid from the Lance Formation of Wyoming dated to 65.5 million years ago.
The genus was initially placed in the wastebin genus Cimolopteryx before Pierce Brodkorb assigned the current name in 1970, after first affiliating it with Apatornis in 1963.
The relationships of Palintropus are poorly determined mainly due to the scarcity of material.

A 2009 cladistic analysis by Longrich and colleagues suggested Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis and belongs in the family Palintropiformes, a conclusion supported by earlier work proposing the newly established group, though other sources assign it to Quercymegapodiidae or the class Reptilia.
In contrast, the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group and family assigned to Palintropus as Quercymegapodiidae and classifies it under the class Reptilia.
Some researchers believe Palintropus is an early member of the Charadriiformes, similar to birds of the Western Interior Seaway, while others note its potential link to subtropical coastlands.
An alternate theory suggests Palintropus is a galliform, possibly a quercymegapodiid, an alternative view that aligns with other classification suggestions.
